projects.title: Portfolio Optimization Using Reinforcement Learning
projects.description:
Major Qualifying Project for Computer Science B.Sc., WPI.

In this report, we analyze the effect of data complexity on the performance of financial reinforcement learning models. We created six models which were identical except for the complexity of their learning data. The goal for each was to make as much money as possible by investing in only a single stock. We trained these models on daily index fund data, intraday index fund data, and daily foreign exchange data. We then analyzed the effect that the different data complexities had on both the training and testing returns. Simpler models cannot learn anything and will perform poorly, while if a model is too complex, the agents will overfit the training data and perform poorly on testing data. State spaces with moderate complexity tend to perform the best.

projects.title: Navigational Kiosk Application (CS 3733)
projects.description:
For my Software Engineering course (CS 3733), I worked as part of a 10-person team with the goal of designing a navigational kiosk application that would be used in a hospital. My position was Full-Time Software Engineer, meaning that my main focus for the 7-week course was designing a robust, working product. My team employed the Agile framework to design the application, with everyone involved in processes like requirements gathering, software development, the daily scrums, and our retrospectives.

Initially, my team split into three main groups: Algorithms; UI; and Database. We were shorthanded for people familiar with SQL, but I opted to learn what I could given the short time frame. Thus I became part of the two-person Database team, and it was truly a great learning experience.

Usually, out of the five or so teams, only one or two winners are decided on at the end of the course. However, our professor and his assistants elected a five-way tie for first place for the first time in the course's history.

Overall, while the work was often difficult and time-consuming, CS 3733 was a very positive experience for me because I learned so much about programming and what it is like to be in that kind of development environment.
